title: Regional Connection Governor: pool spillover and progressive soft-degrade playbook
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Under cross-region pressure and transient downstream degradation (Redis/KV, Kafka, Postgres), our monolithic connection pools and strict fail-fast circuits cause cascading timeouts and tenant-level outages.

Goal: Design and implement a "Connection Governor" playbook that coordinates per-region connection pool spillover, probabilistic circuit annealing, and progressive soft-degradation modes to preserve SLOs for high-priority workloads while maintaining graceful overall system availability. The playbook must include runtime controls, telemetry rollouts, and an automated canary for staged enablement.

Scope: engineering changes to connpool, policy controller for per-tenant priorities, circuit state machine (add GENTLE->COREDOWN transitional state), regional routing fallback hooks, KV cache promotion rules, and operator runbooks for incident response. Excludes UI work for Console dashboards (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Connection Governor integrated into runtime: per-region pool quotas, soft-spill strategy, and priority admission implemented and configurable via feature flags
Circuit breaker extended with GENTLE state: allows probabilistic degraded responses and read-only fallthrough to cached KV for a configurable percentage of requests
Observed improvement under synthetic failure: 40% reduction in tenant error-rate at median latency SLO breach events vs baseline in chaos tests
Automated canary rollout pipeline: enablement in a single region -> two-region cross-validation -> global rollout with automatic rollback on key metric regressions
Operator playbook added to runbook doc with step-by-step mitigation and next actions for persistent dependency degradation
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Alvarez: Initial ticket created after postmortem for incident 2026-03-08 where Redis regional storms caused several tenant 5xx spikes. Proposed concept sketch attached in Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/conn-governor (private).

2026-03-11 Marcus Chen: Spike implementation plan accepted. We'll prototype spillover using a per-region token-bucket and a secondary conservative pool that accepts only priority lanes. Plan to avoid cross-region amplification by bounding outgoing failover rate.
2026-03-11 Priya Natarajan (SRE review): Suggest adding a soft-degradation metric (pct_degraded_responses) and a circuit annealing schedule to avoid immediate hard trip on short-lived latency blips.

2026-03-12 Marcus Chen: Implemented basic GENTLE state in local branch. GENTLE returns cached or truncated responses for non-critical routes with a 15% admission cap. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/9872

2026-03-12 Design review (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed UX hooks required for Console to surface priority lanes and live spillover counts. We'll file Console ticket separately and include metrics exposed via traces and per-route telemetry.

2026-03-12 QA plan added: chaoskit experiment: throttle Redis to 200ms 50% of requests for 10m and compare baseline vs governor-enabled behavior across three regions. Metrics: 99th latency, error-rate, pct_degraded_responses, cross-region egress volume.
notes: Design decisions: prefer probabilistic shedding over strict quiesce to avoid synchronized mass-fallback; use leaky-bucket per-tenant with global cap to prevent tenant blast radius.
Trade-offs: soft-degrade increases returned 'stale' responses; must pair with evals to measure user-perceived regressions (quality vs availability).

Rollout safeguards: monitor pct_degraded_responses, per-tenant error-rate, and cross-region network egress; automatic rollback threshold: >10% absolute increase in tenant error-rate or >25% traffic experiencing degraded responses in canary region.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype per-region governor component + simple GENTLE circuit; unit tests and local benchmarks
Week 2: integrate with connpool, add priority lanes and KV promotion hooks; e2e in staging
Week 3: chaos experiments and metric baselining; iterate on annealing schedule
Week 4: rollout canary, observe, and gradual global enablement if thresholds met
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and admission policies
Integration tests simulating multi-region failover with synthetic Redis/Kafka latency spikes
Chaos experiments with chaoskit to validate behavioral regression targets
Customer-simulated load tests for priority tenants to measure SLO preservation
